exact_original_alert.finding: thm-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-on-manifolds allows zero-dimensional manifolds, but proof 2.1 says 'By [L2] ... the restriction ... is a bijection with C1 inverse', where L2 is thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem, whose Statement begins 'Let n≥1'. Thus the cited theorem does not cover the zero-dimensional case admitted here. For example, an arbitrary map between discrete zero-manifolds has an isomorphism on the zero tangent spaces at every point. The desired local inverse exists on singleton neighbourhoods, but this separate argument is missing.
